translationRepairs: Pu entered princely service at ten. His steadiness won him favor; he was made an acting attendant on the heir's staff and twice promoted to eastern head palace attendant.
Pu entered princely service at ten. His steadiness won him favor; he was made a Jiban attendant and twice promoted to eastern head palace attendant.
寄班祗候 is the Jiban attendant post, not 'an attendant on the heir's staff'.
When the city fell, Wang Jun broke out at midnight through the south gate. Pu pursued him to Fushun and forced him to kill himself; the remaining rebels were pacified.
When the city fell, Wang Jun broke out at midnight through the south gate. Pu pursued him to Fushun, where Wang Jun killed himself; the remaining rebels were pacified.
均自殺 says Wang Jun killed himself; 'forced him to' is not in the source.

During a Khitan border raid he served as Baozhou military supervisor and strategic-planning vanguard on the northern field staff. He fought them at Liangliang city and again at Changcheng pass, taking many prisoners and a large haul of weapons and armor.

During a Khitan border raid he served as Baozhou military supervisor and strategic-planning vanguard on the northern field staff. He fought them at Lianliang city and again at Changcheng pass, taking many prisoners and a large haul of weapons and armor.
After peace was concluded, he was promoted to military commissioner of Rongzhou.
After peace was concluded, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Rongzhou.
觀察使 is a surveillance commissioner, not a military commissioner.
He was reassigned as observer of Guizhou and overall commander on the Zhenzhou circuit, then as acting military commissioner of Baoping, and went to take up his post.
He was reassigned as surveillance commissioner of Guizhou and overall commander on the Zhenzhou circuit, then as acting military commissioner of Baoping, and went to take up his post.
觀察使 is a surveillance commissioner; 'observer' is wrong.
His mother bore him while she was still a commoner; later she entered the palace as wet nurse to the late heir apparent.
His mother bore him while she was still a commoner; later she entered the palace as wet nurse to Heir Apparent Daoxian.
悼獻太子 is the posthumous title Heir Apparent Daoxian; 'the late heir apparent' drops the name.

He became defender of Jizhou and chief of the palace horse guards, then chief commandant before the hall with concurrent observer of Guizhou, and finally deputy overall commander of the palace foot guards.

He became defense commissioner of Jizhou and chief of the palace horse guards, then chief commandant before the hall with concurrent surveillance commissioner of Guizhou, and finally deputy overall commander of the palace foot guards.
防禦使 is a defense commissioner and 觀察使 a surveillance commissioner; 'defender' and 'observer' are wrong.
When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshal with the temple name Qinhuai.
When he died he was posthumously granted the title Grand Commandant and the posthumous name Qinhui.
贈太尉 is a posthumous office (Grand Commandant), not enfeoffment; 諡勤惠 is a posthumous name Qinhui, not a temple name 'Qinhuai'.
When thirty thousand Xia cavalry besieged Chengpu Stockade, Huaide was inside the walls; he led over a thousand elite troops in a breakout and routed the enemy.
When thirty thousand Xia cavalry besieged Chengping Stockade, Huaide was inside the walls; he led over a thousand elite troops in a breakout and routed the enemy.
承平砦 is Chengping Stockade, not 'Chengpu'.

When raiders harried subject Qiang and more than ten camps were lost, he was moved to Yongxing Army, then Gaoyang Pass and the Bingdai circuit, serving in turn as palace front chief commandant, observation commissioner of Suizhou, deputy overall commander of the imperial guards cavalry, Wuxin military commissioner and observation remnant, deputy palace front commander, and military commissioner of Ningyuan.

When raiders harried subject Qiang and more than ten camps were lost, he was moved to Yongxing Army, then Gaoyang Pass and the Bingdai circuit, serving in turn as palace front chief commandant, surveillance commissioner of Suizhou, deputy overall commander of the imperial guards cavalry, acting military commissioner of Wuxin, deputy palace front commander, and military commissioner of Ningyuan.
觀察使 is surveillance commissioner and 節度觀察留後 is acting military commissioner; 'observation remnant' is a literal error.
When a maternal cousin died childless, Huaide tried to seize her land by false claim. Exposed, he lost command of the guards and was made prefect of Bo, then transferred to Xu.
When a younger female cousin died childless, Huaide tried to seize her land by false claim. Exposed, he lost command of the guards and was made prefect of Bo, then transferred to Xu.
從妹 is a younger female cousin on the paternal side; 'maternal' is not in the source.
He died and was posthumously made palace attendant with the temple name Rongyi.
He died and was posthumously made palace attendant with the posthumous name Rongyi.
諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.
After Liu Chang's rebellion in Xichuan was crushed, Shang Guanzheng had debated wall repairs without deciding; Yunze was sent with Wang Chenghan and Yan Chenghan to inspect.
After Liu Gan's rebellion in Xichuan was crushed, Shangguan Zheng had debated wall repairs without deciding; Yunze was sent with Wang Chengkan and Yan Chenghan to inspect.
劉旰 is Liu Gan, 上官正 is Shangguan Zheng (double surname 上官), and 王承衎 is Wang Chengkan.
When He Chengjue, Hebei frontier commissioner and market intendant, fell ill and was told to pick his successor, he named Yunze for Xiong Prefecture.
When He Chengju, Hebei frontier commissioner and market intendant, fell ill and was told to pick his successor, he named Yunze for Xiong Prefecture.
何承矩 is He Chengju; 'Chengjue' misreads 矩.
He became a director of the Court of Judicial Review and recorder at the western capital.
He became assistant of the Court of Judicial Review and recorder at the western capital.
大理寺丞 is the assistant (丞) of the Court of Judicial Review, not its director.
When Yuan Hao rebelled he became Jingyuan military inspector and Wei prefect, then Zhong prefect, then Fuyan inspector and Fu prefect.
When Yuan Hao rebelled he became Jingyuan circuit military supervisor and prefect of Wei, rose to right Qiji commissioner and prefect of Zhong, then moved to the Fuyan circuit as prefect of Fu.
The English omits 右騏驥使 and misrenders the sequence of 鈐轄, 刺史 and 知鄜州.
Zhao Yu's cavalry took a side road while Zhao Zhen mistook him for the enemy on the Gaotou plain and attacked his own man.

Zhao Yu's cavalry advanced first by a side road, while Zhao Zhen and Wang Kui hurried toward Saimen; on the Gaotou plain road a white-horse scout reported the enemy under a blue canopy east of the hills, and Zhen led his men in a surprise attack—only to find it was Yu.
The English omits Wang Kui (王逵), the march to Saimen, and the scout's report; 振麾兵掩襲，乃瑜也 says Zhen attacked and it turned out to be Yu.
Promoted deputy western palace gate chief and overall inspector, he garrisoned Yanzhou.
Promoted to western upper gate commissioner and overall military supervisor, he garrisoned Yanzhou.
西上閤門使 is the commissioner itself, not a deputy; 都鈐轄 is overall military supervisor.
建寧砦 is Jianning Stockade; 'Ning Stockade' drops 建.
The Xia fought him repeatedly at Tumaomao River.
The Xia fought him repeatedly at the Tumao River.
兔毛川 is the Tumao River; 'Tumaomao' duplicates a syllable.
Kang held the main line while Zhang Bian hid thousands of crossbowmen behind the hill.
Kang held the main line while the valiant general Zhang Jie hid several thousand short-weapon troops and crossbowmen behind the hill.
張岊 is Zhang Jie (岊 jié), not 'Zhang Bian'.
When Xia and Khitan fought on the frontier he again became promotion commissioner and Dai prefect with Hebei border duties.
When Xia and Khitan fought on the frontier he again became introducing commissioner and deputy overall commander, prefect of Dai with Hedong border pacification duties.
河東 is Hedong, not Hebei; 引進使 is introducing commissioner.
Pacifying Hedong he raised a hundred twenty thousand militia and rated dozens of local officials.
Pacifying Jingdong he raised a hundred twenty thousand militia and rated dozens of local officials.
京東 is Jingdong, not Hedong.
After a year his governance won praise and he returned to court as giving-the-throne attendant.
After a year his governance won praise and he returned to court as supervising secretary.
給事中 is supervising secretary; 'giving-the-throne attendant' is a literal misreading.
When bandits rose in Hedong he became Yan prefect and cleared them within months.
When bandits rose in Jingdong he became Bureau of Military Affairs academician and prefect of Yunzhou and cleared them within months.
京東 is Jingdong and 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Hedong and Yan; the English also drops 樞密直學士.
Raised in the palace, Taizong made him a left-class attendant and western-head usher.
As a boy he entered the palace with his mother; Taizong made him a left-class hall attendant, then western-head palace attendant and Jiban attendant.
The English omits 從母 (with his mother) and misrenders the offices.
At Wating he smashed the Dangliu clans, killed a fierce chief, and took vast herds.

In the Kangding era, as inspector of Wating Stockade in Weizhou and acting commander of Jingbian Stockade, he smashed the Dangliu and other clans, killed a fierce chief, and took horses, cattle and camels by the ten thousand.
The English drops the Kangding date, his posts and the Jingbian command.
Cowardly Xu Huaide, repeatedly demoted, was no match for Pu.
Xu Huaide, timid and unequal to his duties, was repeatedly demoted and fell far short of Pu.
以懦不任事 means timid and unfit for office; 'Cowardly Xu Huaide' fuses the judgment into his name.
Li Yunze ruled Hebei twenty years so quietly the Khitan called him a elder statesman.
Li Yunze ruled Hebei twenty years so quietly that the Khitan called him an elder.
Grammar: 'a elder statesman' should be 'an elder'; 長者 is 'an elder', not 'statesman'.
Scholar Zhang Kang's victories at Liuli and Tumaomao were thrilling proof that a literatus could win glory.
Scholar Zhang Kang's victories at Liuli and the Tumao River were thrilling proof that a literatus could win glory.
兔毛川 is the Tumao River, not 'Tumaomao'.
